description: An independent, solo-led project by SAH, exploring interplanetary exploration through BEYOND EARTH: The Interplanetary Mission Architect. The project combines astrophysics, spacecraft engineering, orbital mechanics and interactive educational simulation, inspired by NASA's Mars Cube One mission. Developed independently with a focus on scientific research, engineering trade-offs and accessible space education.
summary:
BEYOND EARTH: The Interplanetary Mission Architect is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the engineering decisions behind interplanetary space missions. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's Space Mission Design Game challenge, the project features a Mars Relay mission inspired by NASA's Mars Cube One (MarCO) technology demonstration.

Players configure a simulated spacecraft, select scientific payloads and communication systems, and balance constraints involving mass, power, data capacity, budget and mission duration. Through mission events and an interactive Mission Consequence Engine, players explore how one engineering decision can affect multiple spacecraft subsystems. A post-mission debrief explains design outcomes and highlights areas for improvement.

The project draws on NASA and JPL educational and mission resources to make systems-level aerospace engineering more accessible. Its simplified calculations and game parameters are clearly distinguished from real spacecraft specifications and operational mission predictions.
details:
Project Overview

BEYOND EARTH: The Interplanetary Mission Architect is an independent educational space mission-design simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project focuses on an interplanetary Mars Relay mission inspired by NASA's historic Mars Cube One (MarCO) technology demonstration. It gives users an opportunity to explore the engineering decisions involved in designing and operating a small interplanetary spacecraft.

How It Works

Players begin by understanding their mission objectives and configuring a simulated spacecraft. They select spacecraft components, scientific payloads, power systems and communication equipment while managing important engineering constraints.

The Mission Control interface presents key resources, including spacecraft mass, available power, data capacity, budget and mission feasibility.

The central feature is the Mission Consequence Engine. It demonstrates how changing one engineering parameter can influence several interconnected spacecraft systems. Adding a scientific instrument, for example, can increase scientific capability while introducing additional mass, power and data requirements.

Players can then experience simulated mission events, make operational decisions and evaluate their spacecraft through a post-mission debrief.

Scientific Foundation

The project draws upon NASA and Jet Propulsion Laboratory resources covering CubeSat engineering, the MarCO mission, Mars communications and interplanetary orbital transfers.

It introduces scientific concepts such as the inverse-square relationship governing solar intensity and the communication delays resulting from the immense distance between Earth and Mars.

Historical mission information and published scientific references are distinguished from simplified educational calculations and illustrative simulation parameters.

Innovation and Intended Impact

BEYOND EARTH transforms abstract aerospace engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience. Its aim is to help students and aspiring space enthusiasts understand that successful missions depend on balancing scientific ambition with engineering limitations.

Rather than presenting mission design as a collection of isolated facts, the simulator encourages experimentation, critical thinking, problem-solving and learning through consequences.

Development and Technologies

The application was developed as a browser-based interactive experience using Lovable's AI-assisted web development platform. ChatGPT supported project ideation, research assistance, prompt development and written content.

The application uses a simplified educational simulation model and predefined parameters. It does not provide operational spacecraft engineering certification or control actual spacecraft.

BEYOND EARTH is an independently developed educational project. NASA does not sponsor or endorse the application.
